locator.text: Equation (7.10), p. 75, in the statement of Lemma 7.1

evidence: paper: B^{\ell}(\mathcal{A}_\Phi B - B') = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda, -\lambda) + E, \qquad \lambda(v) = \frac{\lambda_0}{\sqrt{1+s(v)^2}}, \qquad |E| \le C/S_*.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean never forms the 3×2 matrix B, its left inverse B^ℓ, or the product B^ℓ(A_Φ B − B') as objects; it performs the same conjugation entry by entry and names only the result. The dictionary: `FrameData.ambient z w = tangent ρ (frame z) (w0+w1) (h·(w0−w1)) = (w0+w1)(e_r − ρK_a) + h(w0−w1)·(frame z 1)` is the map B, with ρ = radialSlope n = n_{Φ,r}/|n_{Φ,tan}| = s_a and frame z 0 = normalDirection n = K_a of (7.7); h = eigenvector = referenceProfile c0 u L v = c0·√(1+s(v)²), which is the scalar in the second column of (7.8). errorA/errorB/errorC (PrimaryODE.lean 49–58) are the three entries of the operator in the (x,y) coordinates minus their reference values 0, λ/h, λ·h, and `reference_off_diagonal` is the statement that those reference values are the diagonalizable ones; modal11…modal22 (MovingFrameODE.lean 678–681) are their transform into the (p,q) eigenbasis, including the term `rate = h'/h` and the frame rotation, which is where the paper's −B′ enters. `modal_equations_iff`/`hasDerivAt_modal` then say the projected equation in these coordinates has generator diag(λ,−λ) − d + E with E = (modal11, modal12; modal21, modal22), and `modal_errors` bounds each of the four entries by modalConstant M u / D.scale i, so ‖E‖ ≤ 4·C/S_* in operator norm (MovingFrameODE.modal_error_opNorm_le). λ matches exactly: `referenceEigenvalue λ₀ u L v = λ₀/√(1 + slotMagnitude²)` and slotMagnitude² = s(v)² (signedSlot_sq), with D.scale i = S_*. Two conventions differ: (a) the Lean splits E entrywise rather than using a matrix norm; (b) the Lean's second tangent basis vector is `quarterTurn (normalDirection n) = (−(K_a)_z, (K_a)_θ)`, i.e. minus the paper's N_a = ((K_a)_z, −(K_a)_θ), and correspondingly the structure fields `eigen12`/`eigen21` of `FamilyData` force the Lean's c0 to carry the opposite sign to the paper's c0 < 0; the two sign flips cancel in `ambient`, so the first modal eigenvalue is +λ in both. The paper's clause that B^ℓ is uniformly bounded is `FrameData.norm_le_ambient`, stated as a two-sided coordinate bound rather than as a norm of a named matrix.
